tasks.short: Stop production when serious defects threaten product quality or safety.

steps.what: Review failed inspection results in the quality management system {OTHER}.
Inspect the affected process and establish the likely defect extent.
Order an immediate stop and define its production scope.
Halt the affected production equipment using its operating controls.
Place affected batches on hold in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
Record the stop in the quality management system {OTHER}.
Notify planning and warehouse teams of the confirmed stop and holds.

tasks.design: A read-only evidence view joins inspection results from the quality management system {OTHER} to batch records in the {OPS_SYSTEM}. After the manager orders a stop and the supervisor confirms it, configured holds require batch-scope approval, while a deterministic template creates the incident record and sends containment notices through {EMAIL}. Physical stopping remains with trained staff using established operating controls.
tasks.previous_blocker: Defect evidence, batch identity and hold records sit in separate places. The serious-defect decision also depends on conditions at the line.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing hold configuration and modest integration code can connect these records. AI-assisted coding can reduce implementation effort, while established validation remains necessary.
tasks.still_hard: Tracing mixed or reworked batches and judging an unfamiliar defect remain difficult. Any change to equipment controls would need a separate engineering scope.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unsafe situation, challenge uncertain evidence and stop production despite delivery pressure.

ambition.what: Traceable containment status for production planning and warehouse teams

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time copying stop details and answering status requests. Stop and restart authority remain unchanged; restart requires its own established release process.

reach.task: Replan work around held batches
reach.learn: Batch genealogy, stock status and the effect of a hold on downstream orders.

evidence.claim: Structured evidence views, batch-hold workflows and template reports can reduce administrative work around a human stop decision.
Physical containment and unfamiliar serious-defect assessment require site-specific operating knowledge and validation.

assumptions: The company has batch records, electronic inspection results and an existing hold function.
The manager has established stop authority; production staff perform the physical stop.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for one site and one production interface.
Access work includes GDPR controls for identifiable incident records and employee consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which defects require an immediate stop under the site's approved procedures?
Can the existing hold function cover split, mixed and reworked batches?
Which roles may stop production, confirm containment and authorise restart?
Are inspection and batch interfaces available with suitable access?
research_questions: Which sector-specific requirements govern electronic containment records and system validation?
new_work: Resolve missing or conflicting batch links.
Check failed hold writes and notification delivery.
Maintain defect thresholds, recipient lists and access permissions.
Periodically test the administrative workflow against containment procedures.
tasks.statement: Stop production if serious product defects are present.

tasks.short: Review contractor quality plans and approve acceptable controls before work starts.

steps.what: Receive the contractor plan and register its version and review deadline.
Map plan sections to contractual requirements and identify missing information.

loop.input: A versioned contractor plan, approved contract requirements and review checklist.
loop.output: A requirements matrix with source passages and missing evidence.
loop.check: Require valid section references and complete requirement coverage; the reviewer checks material mappings.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass; unreadable sections or ambiguous matches go to the reviewer.
loop.why_not_simpler: Contractors describe equivalent controls using different document structures and terminology.

steps.what: Assess whether proposed controls adequately address technical and contractual risks.
Resolve unclear controls and negotiate necessary plan revisions with the contractor.
Approve the plan, impose conditions or require further revision.
Send the decision and file the approved plan version and conditions.

tasks.design: Configure intake, version control and routing in the {WORKFLOW} and {DOCS}; a bounded reader maps plan evidence to approved requirements from the {CLM}. The quality manager assesses technical adequacy and approves the exact plan version and conditions. That recorded approval releases a templated notice through the {EMAIL} and locks the controlled version.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document variation makes checklist preparation slow, while technical acceptance cannot be reduced to section presence.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can prepare a cited requirements matrix, and existing approval workflows can handle routing and release.
tasks.still_hard: Determining whether controls work in practice, interpreting contract exceptions and resolving disagreements with contractors.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a formally complete plan leaves a material process risk uncontrolled.

ambition.what: A pre-submission completeness check for small contractors.

tasks.altitude: The quality manager receives a prepared requirements matrix and spends more time on consequential control weaknesses. Technical approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Include quality-plan conditions in supplier onboarding and purchasing restrictions.
reach.learn: Supplier master controls, contractual milestones and the distinction between quality approval and purchasing authority.

evidence.claim: Intake, version control, approval routing and notices can use configured workflows.
Cited extraction can assist document review, but section coverage does not establish technical adequacy.

assumptions: Plans arrive mainly as documents, with some clarification by call.
The quality manager has delegated authority to approve plans within defined limits.
Technical judgement retains substantial effort despite the supplied automation prior.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates for one plan family.
GDPR applies to personal data in contractor records; consultation requirements depend on national rules.
unknowns: Contract-specific requirements and permitted approval conditions.
Current document formats, submission volumes and review cycle times.
Whether conditional approval permits work to start.
Existing approval delegation and document retention rules.
Available interfaces, access permissions and consultation requirements.
research_questions: Which completeness checks can be expressed as deterministic rules?
How often does extraction miss a limitation or map evidence to the wrong requirement?
Can approval and outbound release be reliably bound to the same document version?
new_work: Review requirements mappings and extraction exceptions.
Maintain checklists and approved requirement libraries.
Resolve duplicate submissions and version conflicts.
Monitor failed notices and approval-to-release consistency.
tasks.statement: Review and approve quality plans submitted by contractors.

tasks.short: Review quality-control research, technology and regulatory developments.

steps.what: Search regulatory portals and technical publication services for relevant developments.
Screen newsletters and professional updates for additional items.
Read selected publications and note findings, changes, dates and limitations.

loop.input: Retrieved publication text, provenance, version dates and watch scope.
loop.output: Cited brief describing findings, regulatory status, dates, limitations and possible relevance.
loop.check: Require passage references; distinguish proposals from adopted requirements; check dates against source metadata.
loop.stop: One reading pass and one repair pass per publication; unavailable text or uncertain status goes to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technical findings and relevance depend on prose. Metadata filters can narrow the sources but cannot summarise their meaning.

steps.what: Evaluate study quality, statistical assumptions and claimed technology benefits.
Discuss applicability and decide whether a development warrants further investigation.
Update the watch register with decisions, owners and follow-up dates.

tasks.design: Scheduled collection on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reads permitted sources from {GOV_PORTAL}, publication services in {OTHER} and routed updates from {EMAIL}. A bounded reading loop produces cited briefs in {DOCS}, while a register and reminders in {WORKFLOW} track the manager's decisions and follow-up dates.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sources had different formats and access arrangements, and generic alerts generated too much reading without local context.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled collection and bounded summarisation can prepare a focused reading queue. They do not establish legal applicability or scientific validity.
tasks.still_hard: Licensed access, source coverage, evolving regulatory status and transferability of research to local processes remain difficult.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing sound evidence from attractive claims and recognising when local conditions invalidate a published result.

ambition.what: Monthly quality-technology trial shortlist for production engineering

tasks.altitude: The manager reads fewer irrelevant items and spends more time evaluating promising changes with engineering. They can recommend trials sooner; budgets and control changes still require their existing approvals.

reach.task: Compare the expected cost and benefit of proposed quality-technology trials.
reach.learn: Trial evaluation, baseline selection and separating measured benefit from supplier claims.

evidence.claim: Scheduled collection, metadata filtering and deduplication can reduce repeated searching.
Cited summaries support reading but do not replace scientific appraisal or legal applicability decisions.

assumptions: The baseline combines portal searches, newsletters, document reading and a local watch register.
Collection uses permitted feeds, downloads or interfaces; subscription charges are additional to technical running costs.
Build ranges cover a defined source list and one quality domain.
The watch process creates investigation requests; it does not automatically change testing limits or procedures.
GDPR applies to mailbox content and named contacts. Use scoped newsletter access and assess national consultation rules if employee data use changes.
unknowns: Relevant sectors, jurisdictions, standards and product scope.
Current subscriptions, retrieval rights and available source interfaces.
Who confirms regulatory applicability and authorises trials.
Whether mailbox access or new data use requires employee consultation.
research_questions: Which authoritative sources cover the agreed watch scope?
How often does the shortlist miss relevant developments or include irrelevant ones?
Can briefs reliably distinguish research findings, commercial claims and binding requirements?
new_work: Maintain source coverage, retrieval permissions and watch scope.
Check important claims, source passages and regulatory status.
Investigate missed updates, broken collection and inaccessible publications.
Close follow-up items and update trial outcomes.
tasks.statement: Review statistical studies, technological advances, or regulatory standards and trends to stay abreast of issues in the field of quality control.

tasks.short: Prepare, approve and monitor the quality control operating budget.

steps.what: Export quality cost-centre actuals and commitments from the {ERP}.
Reconcile costs and classify recurring or exceptional spending in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Agree workload, staffing, consumables, calibration and maintenance assumptions with operational leads.
Calculate budget scenarios and document funding priorities in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Review trade-offs and approve the quality operating budget.
Enter the approved budget and cost-centre allocations in the {ERP}.
Maintain variance analysis and proposed forecast changes in the {SPREADSHEET}.

tasks.design: Configure scheduled actuals and approved-budget imports in the {ERP}, using a small job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} for mappings and scenario calculations. Keep versioned assumptions and approval records in the {WORKFLOW}, and publish variances in the {BI}. Forecast proposals return through the existing approval route before changing the budget.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cost mappings, assumptions and budget versions sit in separate files. Financial approval remains necessary even when calculations are routine.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured exports and imports can handle standard records. AI coding makes a tailored scenario calculator and reconciliation checks cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Forecasting testing demand and choosing between cost, capacity and quality risk remain uncertain. Poor cost attribution needs finance input.
tasks.human_edge: Defend necessary quality spending and judge the operational consequences of budget reductions.

ambition.what: Monthly quality-capacity reforecast

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling workbooks and more time testing capacity and spending choices with finance. Budget approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess quality cost drivers and compare capacity scenarios.
reach.learn: Cost allocation, sensitivity analysis and the distinction between correlation and causation.

evidence.claim: Budget calculations, account mappings and variance reports can use deterministic rules.
Scenario preparation can be automated while funding trade-offs remain human decisions.

assumptions: The {ERP} holds actuals and approved budgets; a {SPREADSHEET} commonly supports scenario preparation.
Build ranges cover one quality function, an agreed account mapping and existing import facilities.
No model loop is needed for the initial scope.
Only an approved budget version can be imported; imports are logged and checked for duplicates.
Use aggregate staffing costs where possible; GDPR and applicable national consultation rules govern employee data.
unknowns: Whether the {ERP} already provides adequate planning and variance features.
How quality costs, commitments and shared services are allocated.
Whether approved-budget imports are supported.
How often forecasts are reviewed and who may approve changes.
Whether employee-level cost data is necessary and consultation applies.
research_questions: Which workbook adjustments recur and can become explicit mapping rules?
Which operational drivers explain most budget variation?
Would configuring existing planning features remove the need for a separate calculator?
new_work: Review unmapped accounts and reconciliation exceptions.
Maintain cost drivers, rates and scenario assumptions.
Check import totals and budget version controls.
Investigate material variances before proposing forecast changes.
tasks.statement: Generate and maintain quality control operating budgets.

tasks.short: Evaluate whether a new testing or sampling method improves quality control.

steps.what: Define the testing problem, acceptance criteria and practical constraints.
Read method papers, supplier specifications and previous validation reports.

loop.input: An approved document set and evaluation criteria.
loop.output: A cited method comparison with missing evidence marked.
loop.check: Check source passages, units and document versions; the quality manager reviews material claims.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unreadable or conflicting evidence goes to the quality manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Method limitations and applicability appear in varied technical prose.

steps.what: Write a pilot protocol covering samples, controls, analysis and acceptance criteria.

loop.input: Reviewed method comparison, evaluation criteria and protocol template.
loop.output: A draft pilot protocol with unresolved design choices flagged.
loop.check: Validate required sections and referenced limits; the quality manager approves experimental design before execution.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported sample sizes or unresolved safety questions require manual completion.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover structure, but technical prose must reflect the method and testing context.

steps.what: Run pilot tests and record observations, deviations and measurements.
Calculate method performance and compare results against acceptance criteria.
Decide whether to adopt, reject or extend the method trial.
File the approved decision with its supporting evidence.

tasks.design: A bounded reader turns selected evidence in the {DOCS} into a cited comparison and draft protocol. Validated calculations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} feed a {BI} comparison, while the {WORKFLOW} records protocol approval and the adoption decision. Laboratory staff run the trials, and the quality manager decides whether the evidence supports adoption.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technical evidence varies by method, and trustworthy comparisons require experimental design and local validation.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding can reduce the effort of building calculation tools and document workflows. Bounded extraction can prepare evidence without deciding technical suitability.
tasks.still_hard: Representative samples, measurement uncertainty, equipment qualification and proving performance under actual operating conditions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when promising results reflect an unsuitable experiment or fail to address the real quality risk.

ambition.what: Quarterly screening of alternative methods for one recurring test bottleneck.

tasks.altitude: The quality manager spends less time assembling comparisons and filing evidence, and more time designing useful trials. Existing method approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Specify a validated interface for importing laboratory measurements.
reach.learn: Data lineage, units, instrument identifiers and reconciliation of missing measurements.

evidence.claim: Structured performance calculations and versioned evidence workflows can be implemented deterministically.
Technical extraction and protocol drafting need local evaluation; the digest provides no method-validation deployment case.

assumptions: This describes a company with a laboratory or production testing function and controlled documents.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
The first build covers one method family and approved calculations.
Build ranges cover software work; physical trials and qualification may take longer.
GDPR applies to personal data in records; employee consultation depends on national rules and the intended use.
unknowns: Applicable sector standards and customer validation requirements.
Whether existing systems already support method comparison and protocol approval.
Availability and quality of historical measurements and reference samples.
Who has authority to approve protocols and method changes.
Access lead times and any required employee consultation.
research_questions: Which performance calculations and acceptance criteria can be validated once and reused?
How reliably does extraction preserve caveats, units and applicability limits?
Does drafting reduce preparation time after technical review effort is included?
new_work: Review extracted claims and protocol drafts.
Maintain calculation validation and document templates.
Handle missing measurements and contradictory evidence.
Check interfaces after instrument or source-format changes.
tasks.statement: Evaluate new testing and sampling methodologies or technologies to determine usefulness.

tasks.short: Select quality control equipment and coordinate installation, trials and acceptance.

steps.what: Agree measurement needs, operating conditions and acceptance criteria with production and laboratory staff.
Request supplier quotations and collect technical documents through the {EMAIL}.
Compare specifications, lifecycle costs and supplier evidence in a document.

loop.input: Supplier quotations and technical documents against a fixed comparison schema.
loop.output: Cited technical fields, commercial terms and unresolved evidence gaps.
loop.check: Validate units and totals in code; require page references; review every critical specification.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document; unresolved fields stay blank for manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Supplier descriptions and qualifications arrive in inconsistent prose and tables.

steps.what: Run equipment trials using representative samples and document measurement performance.
Choose equipment after reviewing trial results, practical constraints and supplier support.
Raise and approve the purchase order in the {PROCUREMENT}.
Coordinate delivery, installation, training and downtime through the {EMAIL}.
Witness commissioning and authorize equipment use against acceptance criteria.

tasks.design: Configure a selection register in the {WORKFLOW}, linked to supplier documents in the {DOCS} and orders in the {PROCUREMENT}. A bounded extraction loop drafts cited comparisons; deterministic calculations compare costs and flag missing evidence. The {PROJECT} tracks installation dependencies while people conduct trials, select equipment and authorize use.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical trials and supplier-specific evidence resist standardization. Coordination crosses technical, purchasing and production teams.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing approval features and small integrations cover the coordination. AI coding reduces the effort to build comparison tables and evidence checks.
tasks.still_hard: Measurement suitability, representative trials and commissioning remain specialist work. Instrument connections and formal validation can dominate cost.
tasks.human_edge: Recognize misleading trial conditions and judge whether equipment will work reliably on the production floor.

ambition.what: Quarterly measurement-capability investment review

tasks.altitude: The week contains less chasing and comparison assembly, with more time observing trials and resolving capability gaps. Existing equipment acceptance and spending rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Plan equipment commissioning dependencies and production downtime.
reach.learn: Critical paths, installation readiness and change control.

evidence.claim: Configured approvals, structured comparison records and reminders can reduce equipment-selection administration.
Document extraction can draft comparisons, but physical suitability and acceptance need specialist review.

assumptions: A typical company combines technical documents, supplier correspondence, purchasing approvals and physical trials.
Build ranges cover one equipment category and existing connectors; equipment delivery lead time is excluded.
The solution assists measurement decisions and does not operate equipment.
Personal data receives GDPR controls; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which instrument categories and regulated validation requirements apply.
Whether supplier documents and purchasing records have usable identifiers.
Which connections and document access are available.
Who holds purchasing and equipment acceptance authority.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed implementation.
research_questions: Which supplier fields require interpretation rather than direct extraction?
How much coordination time remains after configuring existing approval and reminder features?
Which trial evidence best predicts performance under normal operating conditions?
new_work: Review extracted specifications, units and source references.
Resolve missing supplier evidence and conflicting quotations.
Maintain comparison schemas, approval routes and installation templates.
Check document permissions and integration failures.
tasks.statement: Coordinate the selection and implementation of quality control equipment, such as inspection gauges.

tasks.short: Collect production samples, test them and assess quality against approved specifications.

steps.what: Select the sampling plan for scheduled production.
Collect, label and preserve samples on the production floor.
Test samples using instruments and enter results in the {OTHER} laboratory system.
Copy laboratory results and production identifiers into a comparison workbook.
Calculate specification failures and examine quality trends.
Determine whether results justify acceptance, further testing or a quality hold.

tasks.design: Configure sampling-plan selection and sample records in the {WORKFLOW}, using approved specifications from the {DOCS} and schedules from the {OPS_SYSTEM}. Connect the {OTHER} laboratory system to the {DATA_PLATFORM}; deterministic checks validate identifiers, units and limits, then feed a {BI} exception view. People still collect and test samples, approve sampling changes and authorize quality dispositions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical sampling remained necessary, while laboratory and production records used different identifiers and units. Connecting them required scarce integration and validation effort.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing laboratory configuration and deterministic checks cover much of the paperwork. AI-assisted coding can shorten connector development, but measurement methods still need validation.
tasks.still_hard: Representative sampling, contamination control, destructive tests and interpreting unusual results require practical expertise. Instrument interfaces and validated methods can be expensive to change.
tasks.human_edge: Recognizing an unrepresentative sample or an unreliable measurement before trusting a calculated pass.

ambition.what: Review sampling depth at each shift change when approved procedures permit.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling results and more time investigating weak signals on the floor. Sampling and disposition rights remain within existing delegated authority.

reach.task: Trace held batches through storage and dispatch records.
reach.learn: Batch genealogy, quarantine locations and inventory status controls.

evidence.claim: Structured results can be checked against approved specifications with deterministic code and displayed as exceptions.
Digital records do not remove the physical work or expertise required for representative sampling and valid testing.

assumptions: The company makes physical products and uses laboratory technicians for routine testing.
The {OTHER} laboratory system holds test results; the {OPS_SYSTEM} holds production identifiers.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.
Access work includes GDPR assessment where records identify staff and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which instruments provide supported result exports or interfaces?
Do laboratory and production records share reliable batch identifiers?
Which sampling and disposition decisions may the quality manager approve?
Which validation and employee consultation requirements apply locally?
research_questions: Which approved checks can be configured in existing systems before adding code?
How often do unit errors, missing identifiers and sampling exceptions cause rework?
new_work: Resolve unmatched samples and inconsistent measurement units.
Maintain approved specifications and versioned control limits.
Validate connector changes against known laboratory results.
Review access and retention for identifiable operator records.
tasks.statement: Collect and analyze production samples to evaluate quality.

tasks.short: Audit subcontractor facilities and external laboratories, then verify corrective action.

steps.what: Prepare the audit scope and checklist from requirements and previous findings.

loop.input: Approved requirements, previous findings and an audit checklist.
loop.output: A cited draft audit pack with proposed areas of focus.
loop.check: Check mandatory coverage and source versions; the auditor confirms scope and sampling priorities.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing requirements or conflicting findings require manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Previous findings contain contextual prose that must be related to the current audit scope.

steps.what: Arrange site access, attendance and evidence requests with the subcontractor.
Inspect facilities, observe work, interview staff and sample laboratory or production records.
Discuss findings with site management and resolve factual disagreements.
Write the audit report and link findings to requirements and evidence.

loop.input: Auditor notes, evidence references, clarified facts and applicable requirements.
loop.output: A draft report with cited findings and missing evidence flagged.
loop.check: Every finding must cite supplied evidence and a requirement; the auditor checks wording and factual accuracy.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported findings return to the auditor without invented evidence.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative observations need careful synthesis into clear, evidence-linked findings.

steps.what: Approve finding severity, the audit conclusion and release of the report.
Register corrective actions, send the approved report and chase overdue responses.
Review corrective evidence and decide whether closure or another inspection is justified.

tasks.design: Use the {DOCS} and bounded drafting loops to prepare audit packs and evidence-linked reports. Configure the {WORKFLOW}, {CALENDAR} and {PROJECT} for agreed appointments, approved report release and corrective-action reminders. Auditors inspect the site, discuss findings and verify closure; the quality manager approves report release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Site conditions and evidence credibility require direct observation, while audit paperwork spans documents, calendars and action lists.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured workflows can remove coordination work, and bounded drafting can reuse recorded evidence. Physical inspection still needs experienced people.
tasks.still_hard: Detecting staged compliance, choosing representative records and proving corrective actions remain effective.
tasks.human_edge: Following an unexpected observation, testing explanations and judging whether actual practice matches documented controls.

ambition.what: A focused remote follow-up review between scheduled site audits.

tasks.altitude: Auditors spend less time arranging visits and formatting reports, with most inspection and judgement time retained. Existing audit and closure decision rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Translate critical subcontractor findings into disruption scenarios and fallback plans.
reach.learn: Recovery dependencies, alternate capacity and thresholds for escalating supplier failure risk.

evidence.claim: Scheduling, action tracking and reminders can be handled by configured workflows.
Document preparation can be assisted, while physical inspection and evidence credibility require human judgement.

assumptions: This describes a scheduled supplier audit with a site visit and subsequent corrective-action review.
Routine scheduling automation uses agreed audit windows and templates; contested access goes to a coordinator.
Report transmission occurs only after approval of the exact report version.
Time shares and savings are estimates; travel is excluded because site distance varies.
GDPR applies to identifiable staff evidence. National rules may require consultation when recording or monitoring practices change.
AI Act obligations depend on intended use; this design does not score individual workers.
unknowns: Applicable audit standards, accreditation requirements and contractual access rights.
Whether site rules permit electronic notes, photographs or remote evidence review.
Required audit independence and approval delegation.
Current action-tracking tools and evidence retention periods.
Worker data access restrictions and required consultation.
Whether remote follow-up is acceptable for the relevant finding types.
research_questions: Which findings require another site visit rather than document-based closure?
Does report drafting preserve uncertainty and avoid overstating observed evidence?
Can existing scheduling and action-tracking configuration meet the need without custom code?
new_work: Review generated audit packs and report drafts.
Maintain requirement mappings and report templates.
Handle scheduling exceptions and failed reminders.
Manage evidence access, retention and redaction.
Check that corrective-action records match approved findings.
tasks.statement: Audit and inspect subcontractor facilities including external laboratories.

tasks.short: Verify that incoming materials, components, samples and finished goods meet inspection and testing standards.

steps.what: Retrieve the applicable inspection plan and specification from {DOCS}.
Identify samples, inspect products and measure properties using {OTHER} laboratory equipment.
Compare results against requirements in the {OTHER} quality management system.
Investigate ambiguous results and exceptions in the {OTHER} quality management system.
Approve release, hold or rejection in the {OTHER} quality management system.
Transfer the approved disposition to batch status in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Configure the {OTHER} quality management system to select versioned inspection requirements, check structured results and assemble an exception queue. An integration updates the {OPS_SYSTEM} only from an authorised disposition, preserving batch identity and an audit trail; physical inspection and disposition decisions remain with qualified people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Product revisions, sampling requirements and batch identity were not consistently linked. Physical tests and ambiguous defects also resist a general software solution.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rule engines and controlled records can handle requirement selection and numeric checks. Small integrations are easier to build, but measurement and release validation still take work.
tasks.still_hard: Measurement uncertainty, destructive sampling, cosmetic defects and whether a result represents the whole batch.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise an unusual defect, question an apparently passing result and accept responsibility for disposition.

ambition.what: Daily supplier-lot containment review

tasks.altitude: Inspectors spend less time finding requirements and copying statuses. The quality manager spends more time on exceptions; release rights do not expand.

reach.task: Prepare a supplier quality claim from rejected incoming lots.
reach.learn: Supplier traceability, acceptance terms and the evidence needed to support a claim.

evidence.claim: Versioned inspection plans, numeric acceptance checks and approved batch-status transfers can use deterministic software.
Physical inspection and interpretation of uncertain results remain substantial work; the digest supplies no matching implementation case.

assumptions: The task includes work performed by inspectors under the manager's responsibility.
The existing quality management system supports versioned specifications and configurable acceptance checks.
No new robotic inspection, machine vision or laboratory hardware is included.
Time and build ranges are estimates; regulated validation could require additional work.
Access assessment includes GDPR and any national consultation rules where inspection records identify staff.
unknowns: Applicable product standards, customer requirements and authorised release roles.
Which inspections are instrumented, visual, destructive or performed externally.
How specification revisions and batch genealogy are currently controlled.
Whether approved dispositions already update stock status automatically.
research_questions: How should acceptance checks account for measurement uncertainty near specification limits?
Which failure-recovery design prevents partial or duplicate disposition updates across systems?
new_work: Maintain versioned specifications and sampling rules.
Resolve missing results, invalid equipment status and ambiguous batch identity.
Reconcile failed status transfers.
Validate changed rules and periodically test that unapproved results cannot release stock.
tasks.statement: Verify that raw materials, purchased parts or components, in-process samples, and finished products meet established testing and inspection standards.

tasks.short: Review quality evidence for regulatory submissions and inspections.

steps.what: Confirm the submission or inspection scope and required evidence.
Retrieve controlled documents and records from {DOCS} and the quality management system {OTHER}.
Check required records, dates, signatures and versions against the evidence checklist.
Review whether the evidence supports required claims and identify contradictions.

loop.input: A fixed evidence bundle and the manager-approved requirement list.
loop.output: Proposed claim-to-evidence links, contradictions and unsupported claims with record references.
loop.check: Verify record identifiers, versions and quotations; the manager decides whether each claim is supported.
loop.stop: At most two passes and 20 records per checklist section; unresolved or larger sections go to manual review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Evidence sufficiency and contradictions depend on narrative meaning beyond metadata and checklist presence.

steps.what: Resolve evidence gaps with process owners and agree necessary corrections.
Approve the reviewed evidence pack or return it for further work.
Release the approved evidence pack to the regulatory team through {DOCS}.

tasks.design: A deterministic evidence builder gathers approved versions from {DOCS} and the quality management system {OTHER}, then checks required metadata and creates a traceable index. A bounded loop proposes claim-to-evidence links and contradictions for specialist review; {WORKFLOW} releases the pack internally only after approval, with external submission handled by the authorised regulatory role.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence retrieval and completeness checks span document stores and operational records. Substantive review depends on specialist interpretation, so assembly and judgement have remained intertwined.
tasks.enabler_now: Stable record references and deterministic checks can automate assembly. Bounded text comparison can prepare review findings without deciding regulatory acceptability.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting applicable requirements, assessing weak evidence and handling disputed records remain specialist work. Regulated environments may require substantial system validation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when apparently complete evidence does not substantiate a claim, and defend a candid account of unresolved gaps.

ambition.what: Pre-inspection evidence-readiness review for process owners

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time locating files and more time challenging weak claims before inspection. Regulatory sign-off and external submission rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate inspection-readiness milestones
reach.learn: Evidence dependencies, approval lead times and how unresolved gaps affect the critical path.

evidence.claim: Record identifiers, version metadata and explicit checklists support deterministic evidence assembly and completeness checks.
A bounded model can prepare cited evidence findings, but specialist review is needed to assess regulatory sufficiency.

assumptions: The evidence scope is approved by a qualified person before automated retrieval.
Source records retain version history and can be referenced without overwriting originals.
Time shares and build ranges cover one evidence-pack type; extensive regulated-system qualification would expand the scope.
Access work includes GDPR review of personal data, confidential-record permissions and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Which sector, regulator and submission types apply?
Who may approve evidence packs and submit them externally?
Are signatures, versions and retention metadata available electronically?
What personal or confidential information must be restricted or redacted?
Which validation procedures apply to changes in the evidence workflow?
research_questions: Which current sector rules define evidence admissibility, electronic signatures and retention?
What validation evidence is required for automated document retrieval and model-assisted review?
new_work: Review proposed evidence links and unsupported claims.
Maintain requirement mappings and completeness rules.
Handle unreadable records, conflicting versions and failed retrievals.
Retain source snapshots and review logs for reproducibility.
Revalidate affected workflow components when requirements or interfaces change.
tasks.statement: Review quality documentation necessary for regulatory submissions and inspections.

tasks.short: Review, revise and issue controlled operating procedures and quality manuals.

steps.what: Retrieve the current procedure and its linked change evidence from {DOCS}.
Compare the procedure with change evidence and identify affected sections.

loop.input: The controlled procedure and a fixed bundle of approved change evidence.
loop.output: Affected sections, proposed change reasons and source references.
loop.check: Verify source references and quoted text; the manager checks omissions and applicability.
loop.stop: At most two passes per procedure, with a 20-page input cap; larger or unresolved sections return to the manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Changed operational meaning is expressed in prose and cannot be located reliably through field matching.

steps.what: Agree workable process changes with operators and the process owner.
Draft the revised procedure and its change summary.

loop.input: The current procedure, agreed change scope and cited evidence.
loop.output: A marked-up procedure draft and section-level change summary.
loop.check: Check template structure, preserved limits and source references; the manager checks technical instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision per procedure; unsupported instructions are flagged for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Clear instructions must combine approved changes with existing prose; templates alone cannot express the changes.

steps.what: Approve the technical content, effective date and training requirements.
Publish the approved version and withdraw superseded copies in {DOCS}.
Assign required learning and acknowledgements in the {LMS}.

tasks.design: Configure version control, approval, publication and withdrawal in {DOCS}, with approved training requirements passed to {LMS}. Two bounded loops map change evidence to sections and draft revisions with source references; the manager and process owner settle operational changes before an authorised person approves publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document control can manage versions, but comparing narrative evidence and rewriting instructions still takes specialist attention. Links between incidents, procedure sections and learning assignments are often maintained manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded language-model drafting can handle prose within an approved evidence bundle. Existing document workflows and faster integration development can connect release and training steps.
tasks.still_hard: Confirming that instructions work at the line, resolving conflicting requirements and withdrawing printed copies still require local effort.
tasks.human_edge: Translate process knowledge into instructions that operators can safely follow, and challenge changes that look sound only on paper.

ambition.what: Role-specific briefings for approved procedure changes

tasks.altitude: The manager spends more of the review cycle testing instructions with operators and less time assembling revisions. Approval rights remain unchanged; saved preparation time supports practical change briefings.

reach.task: Maintain controlled workplace procedures
reach.learn: Document ownership, retention schedules and how to withdraw obsolete copies.

evidence.claim: Configured document workflows can enforce version status, approval and release conditions.
A bounded model loop can propose cited procedure revisions, while technical suitability still needs human review.

assumptions: Controlled procedures and change evidence are available as readable electronic documents.
The company already defines authorised approvers and training-assignment rules.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one procedure family and one release workflow.
Access work includes GDPR review of learning records and consultation under national rules where applicable.
unknowns: Does {DOCS} support controlled versions, withdrawal and approval records?
Who must approve each procedure family?
How many controlled paper copies exist?
Can approved role mappings drive assignments in the {LMS}?
What validation and retention requirements apply to these documents?
research_questions: Which sector-specific rules govern electronic approvals, document retention and proof of training?
new_work: Review draft changes and check omitted requirements.
Maintain evidence links, templates and drafting instructions.
Resolve failed publication or learning-assignment transfers.
Check that withdrawn copies disappear from operational use.
tasks.statement: Review and update standard operating procedures or quality assurance manuals.

tasks.short: Prepare quality reports covering nonconformance, production results, root causes and trends.

steps.what: Retrieve production totals, test results and open nonconformance records.
Reconcile counts, calculate quality metrics and resolve reporting gaps.
Discuss incidents with production and engineering to assess causes and corrective actions.
Write the report with charts, incident summaries and supported explanations.

loop.input: Validated metrics, approved root cause assessments, corrective actions and source record identifiers.
loop.output: Narrative sections with record citations; tables and charts are generated deterministically.
loop.check: Validate every number against supplied metrics, verify record citations and require unknown causes to remain unresolved.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per report section; unsupported text is removed and assigned for manual writing.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover routine figures, but incident narratives vary. The loop summarizes recorded findings without determining causes.

steps.what: Review conclusions, unresolved causes and action commitments before approving the report.
Send the approved report to its internal distribution list.
File the approved version and its supporting evidence.

tasks.design: Scheduled integrations on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconcile production and laboratory records, calculate approved metrics and generate charts. A bounded drafting loop assembles cited narrative sections in the {DOCS}; the quality manager approves conclusions before the {WORKFLOW} files the evidence pack and sends internal notifications through the {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data extraction, metric reconciliation and document assembly crossed several systems. Variable incident narratives resisted simple report templates.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable connectors and report generators reduce assembly work. A bounded model loop can summarize supplied findings while deterministic checks protect figures and references.
tasks.still_hard: Poor denominators, late results and changing defect definitions can mislead a polished report. Establishing root causes still requires investigation rather than plausible prose.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguishing a supported cause from a convenient explanation and challenging ineffective corrective actions.

ambition.what: Hold a daily corrective-action priority review using refreshed quality evidence.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from report assembly toward testing explanations and assessing corrective-action effectiveness. Faster reporting adds no automatic authority over production decisions.

reach.task: Evaluate whether corrective actions reduce recurring defects.
reach.learn: Comparable cohorts, stable metric definitions and limits of causal inference.

evidence.claim: Deterministic report generation can handle calculations, charts and document assembly from validated structured records.
A bounded model loop can draft cited incident summaries, but source checks and human approval remain necessary.
The supplied digest provides no sourced quality-reporting product or documented quality-reporting case.

assumptions: Production records sit in the {OPS_SYSTEM}; laboratory and quality records use an {OTHER} laboratory or quality system.
Routine reports are internal; external disclosures follow a separate approval route.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates.
Access work includes GDPR controls and consultation under national rules if reporting introduces employee monitoring.
unknowns: Which metric definitions and reporting cutoffs are formally approved?
Which reports require signatures, validated software or fixed retention periods?
How much root cause evidence exists before report drafting starts?
Can source records be cited through stable identifiers?
research_questions: Which report sections are fixed templates and which require original analysis?
What reconciliation failures appear when a historical reporting period is replayed?
new_work: Review unsupported statements and missing source evidence.
Resolve reconciliation exceptions before reporting.
Maintain metric definitions, templates and source mappings.
Evaluate drafting quality after material prompt or model changes.
tasks.statement: Produce reports regarding nonconformance of products or processes, daily production quality, root cause analyses, or quality trends.

tasks.short: Help define measurable, feasible and controlled product quality specifications.

steps.what: Gather customer requirements, standards and existing specification documents.

loop.input: Selected customer requirements, applicable standards and approved specifications.
loop.output: Requirements register with source, revision, clause and unresolved conflicts.
loop.check: Verify references exist; preserve quoted limits and units; quality manager confirms completeness and applicability.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per document set; unreadable or conflicting clauses go to review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requirements arrive as varied prose and tables; fixed field mappings cannot reliably capture obligations.

steps.what: Compare proposed requirements with historical test results and process capability.
Draft acceptance criteria, sampling requirements and test-method references.

loop.input: Reviewed requirements, capability comparison, approved test methods and specification template.
loop.output: Specification draft with referenced criteria and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Check units, required fields and traceability; forbid invented limits or methods; quality manager reviews technical meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per specification; unresolved criteria remain flagged for the design review.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates fill fixed fields, but reconciling differently worded requirements needs bounded language interpretation.

steps.what: Resolve quality, cost and manufacturability trade-offs with the product team.
Review trial evidence and assess whether proposed criteria are measurable and achievable.
Approve the specification after required technical and quality sign-offs.
Publish the approved revision and withdraw superseded copies.

tasks.design: Build a requirements register in the {WORKFLOW}, linking clauses in the {DOCS} to deterministic capability comparisons from the {DATA_PLATFORM}. Bounded extraction and drafting loops prepare a referenced specification for technical review. After the authorised sign-offs, configured publication updates the {DOCS} and the {OTHER} quality records system.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements were scattered across documents, and tracing each criterion to evidence took specialist effort. Existing templates did little to resolve inconsistent wording.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding lowers the cost of traceability checks and comparison tools. Bounded extraction can structure prose, while deterministic checks preserve units, revisions and required fields.
tasks.still_hard: Commercial trade-offs, measurement uncertainty and unproven process capability require technical judgement. Access rights to standards and formal change-validation requirements can limit implementation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a plausible requirement is untestable, unsafe or commercially unacceptable.

ambition.what: An early specification feasibility review for prototype teams before production trials.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time assembling clauses and more time challenging testability before design decisions harden. The role gains earlier influence through feasibility reviews; formal specification approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Add specification readiness and unresolved validation questions to project decision points.
reach.learn: Learn dependency planning, change control and how delayed requirements affect trial schedules.

reach.task: Assess whether suppliers can meet proposed acceptance criteria.
reach.learn: Learn supplier qualification evidence, contractual commitments and incoming inspection constraints.

evidence.claim: Requirements traceability, numerical comparisons and revision publication can use deterministic records and workflows.
Language extraction can assist specification drafting but does not establish technical feasibility or regulatory conformity.

assumptions: The quality manager contributes to a cross-functional specification process rather than approving every product alone.
Historical test results are available from the {OTHER} laboratory or quality records system.
Only authorised copies of standards and customer documents enter the drafting process.
Build ranges cover one product family and its existing approval route.
unknowns: Which product standards and sector-specific approval requirements apply.
Who holds each technical, quality and commercial sign-off right.
Whether historical measurements support valid capability comparisons.
Which document licences permit automated processing.
Whether the change affects staff duties enough to require consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can configured document metadata and approval routes provide the register without a separate application?
Which document formats cause missed limits, footnotes or conflicting requirements?
How should comparisons flag unstable processes or inadequate measurement systems?
new_work: Review extracted requirements and resolve conflicting clauses.
Maintain traceability, templates and approved calculation methods.
Check drafts for unsupported limits and omitted conditions.
Maintain source permissions and validate publication behaviour.
tasks.statement: Participate in the development of product specifications.

tasks.short: Monitor product development and pilot production to identify risks before scaling.

steps.what: Read design changes, specifications and development milestones.

loop.input: Current and previous approved specifications, design change records and development milestones.
loop.output: A cited brief of changed requirements, missing evidence and questions for pilot review.
loop.check: Verify document versions and citations; copy numerical requirements exactly and label inferred questions separately.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per change pack; missing or conflicting source material goes to the quality manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Metadata checks handle versions, but varied technical prose needs contextual reading to identify relevant changes.

steps.what: Observe prototypes and pilot runs with production and engineering staff.
Review pilot yield, test results and process variation against requirements.
Update manufacturing risks, evidence gaps and proposed trials in the risk workbook.
Review scale-up risks with engineering and production, then recommend further trials.
Approve the next production stage or require more evidence.
Chase overdue trial results and unresolved quality actions.

tasks.design: A bounded extraction loop prepares cited change briefs from the {DOCS}, while deterministic jobs on the {DATA_PLATFORM} compare pilot results from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and the {OTHER} laboratory system. Configure risk records, trial ownership and reminders in the {PROJECT}, with a {BI} view of missing evidence and unresolved risks. People observe pilot runs, choose experiments and approve production-stage decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Development evidence was scattered across changing documents, pilot records and project discussions. Assessing scale-up risk could not be reduced to checking specification limits.
tasks.enabler_now: Document extraction can make changes easier to review, while deterministic comparisons and linked risk records reduce preparation work. These methods organize evidence without claiming to predict every scale-up failure.
tasks.still_hard: Small pilot runs may not reveal production-scale variation, equipment interactions or supplier variability. Useful experiments require engineering judgement and available trial capacity.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting how a promising prototype could fail under real production constraints and choosing a revealing trial.

ambition.what: Reprioritize pilot experiments after each trial batch.

tasks.altitude: The manager arrives at reviews with current evidence and spends more time designing useful trials. Production-stage approval remains with the designated decision maker; no new release authority is assumed.

reach.task: Link unresolved quality evidence to development milestones.
reach.learn: Critical-path dependencies, stage criteria and evidence-based escalation.

reach.task: Reserve trial capacity without disrupting committed production.
reach.learn: Capacity constraints, changeover requirements and trial lead times.

evidence.claim: Versioned document extraction and linked risk records can reduce preparation effort without determining manufacturing readiness.
Pilot comparisons can identify measured exceptions, but extrapolating to mass production requires engineering judgement.

assumptions: Development uses pilot runs and recorded stage decisions.
The {OTHER} laboratory system holds test results, and document versions are identifiable.
The production manager approves stage progression in this representative setup.
Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates; access work covers confidential designs, GDPR where applicable and consultation under national rules where required.
unknowns: Who has final authority for production-stage progression?
How consistently are design changes linked to pilot batches and test results?
Which readiness criteria are mandatory for the company's products?
How much trial capacity is available between development reviews?
research_questions: Which past scale-up failures were visible in pilot evidence but missed during review?
Can document extraction reliably distinguish approved requirements from proposals?
Which evidence gaps most often delay production-stage decisions?
new_work: Check extracted changes against approved document versions.
Maintain links between risks, pilot batches, experiments and decisions.
Resolve missing or incomparable pilot results.
Review reminder rules and close obsolete risks after design changes.
tasks.statement: Monitor development of new products to help identify possible problems for mass production.

tasks.short: Explain quality requirements to suppliers and agree how deficiencies will be corrected.

steps.what: Retrieve current quality procedures and relevant nonconformance records from the {DOCS}.
Prepare supplier-specific instructions and examples in a document.

loop.input: Approved procedures, relevant nonconformance records and a fixed instruction template.
loop.output: Supplier-specific explanation with procedure versions and record references.
loop.check: Require citations for technical claims; compare limits and test steps with approved procedures.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported claims or conflicting procedures go to the quality manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining how a specific deficiency relates to a procedure requires reading narrative evidence.

steps.what: Check technical accuracy and release the supplier instructions.
Explain testing procedures and demonstrate required practices to supplier representatives.
Resolve practical questions and agree corrective actions, owners and evidence deadlines.
Record attendance, agreed actions and follow-up dates in the {PROJECT}.

tasks.design: Configure a supplier instruction workflow in the {WORKFLOW}, drawing only current procedures and linked records from the {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop prepares cited explanations for technical approval, while people conduct instruction and agree corrective actions. Approved action fields create follow-ups in the {PROJECT}; completing a reminder never closes a deficiency automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier situations differ, and technical guidance carries consequences. Preparation and follow-up are often bundled with the conversation that requires expertise.
tasks.enabler_now: Versioned retrieval and template generation can support preparation. A bounded drafting loop can explain narrative deficiencies using approved source material.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier understanding, practical feasibility and proof of correction need direct assessment. Drafts must not introduce new limits or unapproved testing methods.
tasks.human_edge: Detect misunderstanding, demonstrate good practice and negotiate corrective actions the supplier can actually deliver.

ambition.what: Targeted supplier refresher clinics for recurring test failures

tasks.altitude: Preparation and action logging shrink, leaving more time for demonstrations and supplier problem-solving. The manager retains existing authority over technical guidance and corrective-action acceptance.

reach.task: Prioritize supplier development using recurring quality deficiencies.
reach.learn: Supplier segmentation, delivery constraints and development planning.

evidence.claim: Controlled document retrieval and templated follow-ups can automate supplier instruction administration.
Cited drafting can assist technical explanations while release and corrective-action decisions remain human.

assumptions: Current procedures have identifiable owners and versions.
Build ranges cover one supplier group and one instruction language.
Meeting outputs are entered through structured fields; recording or transcription is outside the initial scope.
Supplier contact data receives GDPR controls; employee consultation follows applicable national rules.
unknowns: Where current procedures and nonconformance records are held.
Whether supplier training requires physical demonstrations.
Which languages and technical qualifications are needed.
Who may approve guidance and agree corrective actions.
Whether suppliers can access a shared action register.
research_questions: Which instruction sections can use approved fixed text without a model?
Which drafting errors would change a test method or acceptance limit?
How will supplier understanding and later corrective-action effectiveness be checked?
new_work: Check draft instructions against current procedures and source records.
Maintain approved examples and instruction templates.
Resolve missing references and conflicting procedure versions.
Review overdue actions and assess evidence of correction.
tasks.statement: Instruct vendors or contractors on quality guidelines, testing procedures, or ways to eliminate deficiencies.

tasks.short: Investigate quality problems and recommend evidence-based improvements.

steps.what: Review defect trends, complaints and previous corrective actions.
Assemble incident histories and supporting records for the selected problems.

loop.input: Selected incident records, inspection records, complaint narratives and corrective action histories.
loop.output: Investigation brief with chronology, record references, contradictions and missing evidence.
loop.check: Validate record identifiers and dates; require references for factual claims; analyst checks completeness and removes personal details.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction pass per investigation; unresolved contradictions remain visible for human investigation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured queries gather records, but incident narratives contain relevant context in varied free text.

steps.what: Observe the process, question staff and test competing explanations.
Compare improvement options using cost, defect impact and implementation assumptions.
Discuss feasibility and recommend a preferred improvement with process owners.
Decide whether to authorise a controlled improvement trial.
Record the decision, owner and effectiveness review date.

tasks.design: Use the {BI} to combine approved quality measures with complaint and corrective-action records from the {HELPDESK} and the {OTHER} quality records system. A bounded loop prepares referenced investigation briefs, while deterministic comparisons on the {DATA_PLATFORM} show costs and explicit assumptions. Human investigation and trial approval feed assignments and effectiveness reviews in the {PROJECT}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Evidence sat in separate records and narratives, so preparing an investigation consumed time. Root-cause judgement could not be reduced to reporting rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Reusable queries, scenario calculations and workflow configuration are cheaper to build with coding assistance. Bounded extraction helps assemble narrative evidence without claiming to establish causation.
tasks.still_hard: Correlation does not establish cause, and production trials may be disruptive. Reliable recommendations need measurement discipline, staff trust and credible estimates of operational impact.
tasks.human_edge: Elicit uncomfortable facts without blame, challenge attractive explanations and negotiate a workable intervention.

ambition.what: Weekly selection of a controlled trial for a recurring quality problem.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends less time constructing evidence packs and can bring a trial recommendation to a weekly decision meeting. Trial spending and process-change approval remain with the authorised operations manager.

reach.task: Evaluate whether an improvement caused a measurable operational benefit.
reach.learn: Learn comparison design, confounding, baseline selection and uncertainty in benefit estimates.

reach.task: Turn an approved improvement trial into a scoped plan with an effectiveness review.
reach.learn: Learn trial dependencies, resource commitments and clear completion criteria.

evidence.claim: Dashboards, referenced evidence packs and deterministic option comparisons can support quality investigations.
Root-cause conclusions and improvement benefits require investigation and validation beyond narrative summarisation.

assumptions: The scope runs from problem selection through recommendation, trial approval and handoff.
The {OTHER} quality records system stores corrective actions, while the {HELPDESK} holds complaint details.
The {SPREADSHEET} currently supports option comparisons using exports and analyst assumptions.
Build ranges assume reusable quality data feeds; establishing those feeds adds work if absent.
unknowns: Which incident, complaint and cost records can be linked reliably.
Who can approve trials, expenditure and process changes.
Whether existing data support credible before-and-after comparisons.
Whether narratives contain personal or sensitive information.
Which national consultation rules apply to changed work practices or employee-linked analysis.
research_questions: Which recurring problems have sufficient evidence for a useful controlled trial?
Can current {BI} and {PROJECT} configuration cover selection, comparison and follow-up?
How often do draft briefs omit contradictory evidence or confuse hypotheses with established facts?
new_work: Review investigation briefs for omissions and unsupported causal language.
Maintain cost assumptions, comparison methods and evidence links.
Resolve access failures and minimise personal information under GDPR.
Follow up trial outcomes and record ineffective or harmful interventions.
tasks.statement: Identify quality problems or areas for improvement and recommend solutions.

tasks.short: Teach staff quality control procedures and verify practical competence.

steps.what: Identify procedure changes and staff needing instruction.
Prepare explanations, demonstrations and practice exercises.

loop.input: Training brief and approved procedure, including revision identifiers.
loop.output: Instruction guide with source references and practice exercises.
loop.check: Require source references for procedural claims; quality manager checks safety, sequence and acceptance criteria.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass per guide; unresolved claims return to manual preparation.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates structure the guide, but explaining procedure changes requires reading and rewriting free text.

steps.what: Arrange attendance around shifts and equipment availability.
Demonstrate procedures, supervise practice and answer questions.
Assess practical competence and decide whether further supervision is needed.
Record completion, procedure revision and any required follow-up.

tasks.design: Configure the {LMS} to connect procedure revisions in the {DOCS} with training assignments, scheduling and completion records. A bounded drafting loop prepares referenced instruction guides for approval; practical teaching and competence decisions stay with the quality manager.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedure revisions, training assignments and competence records were maintained separately. Preparing useful explanations still required specialist time.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing assignment rules handle scheduling and records. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of connecting revisions, while a bounded model loop drafts explanations from approved material.
tasks.still_hard: Practical competence depends on observed technique, equipment and unusual operating conditions. GDPR applies to staff records; consultation requirements depend on national rules and the proposed change.
tasks.human_edge: Notice unsafe habits, adapt explanations and distinguish confidence from demonstrated competence.

ambition.what: Revision-specific refresher sessions for night-shift technicians currently missed between scheduled courses.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less scheduling and guide preparation, with more time for supervised practice across shifts. Existing competence sign-off rights remain; no additional formal authority is assumed.

reach.task: Schedule training around production capacity and shift coverage.
reach.learn: Understand staffing constraints, equipment downtime and the production planning cycle.

evidence.claim: Revision-linked assignments and completion records are suitable for configured workflows; practical competence assessment remains human.
Drafting support and build ranges are estimates, not demonstrated outcomes for this occupation.

assumptions: A typical company has approved procedures in the {DOCS} and training records in the {LMS}.
Procedure identifiers and role requirements can be mapped without automated employee performance scoring.
The new-group ambition applies where night-shift refresher coverage is incomplete.
Build ranges cover one initial training workflow; consultation may exceed the estimated range.
unknowns: Whether the {LMS} supports revision-specific assignments and practical sign-offs.
Who may approve competence for each procedure.
Which shifts currently lack refresher coverage.
Which national rules, worker consultation duties and record-retention requirements apply.
research_questions: Can configured assignment and scheduling features cover the workflow before adding code?
How reliably do draft guides preserve mandatory warnings and procedural sequence?
new_work: Review generated instruction guides against approved revisions.
Resolve scheduling conflicts and failed assignment synchronisation.
Maintain procedure-to-role mappings and access permissions.
Check that completion records reflect approved competence decisions.
tasks.statement: Instruct staff in quality control and analytical procedures.

tasks.short: Identify manufacturing control points and specify sampling procedures.

steps.what: Collect process maps, defect histories and production data.
Walk the production process with operators and observe failure opportunities.
Assess failure severity, detectability and control-point placement with production and laboratory leads.
Calculate sample sizes and frequencies against risk, variation and testing capacity.
Write the sampling plan with locations, frequencies, methods and escalation rules.
Approve the sampling plan in the quality management system.

tasks.design: A job on the {DATA_PLATFORM} collects evidence from the {OPS_SYSTEM} and {DOCS}; a deterministic calculator produces sampling options from approved statistical rules. A template generator prepares the plan in {DOCS}, while the quality manager chooses control points and approves release through the quality management system in {OTHER}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Process evidence was scattered, and sampling calculations and document assembly required local templates and specialist setup.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of building connectors, calculators and templates. The statistical methods already exist.
tasks.still_hard: Representative data, correlated defects, destructive tests and poorly understood failure modes limit reliable sampling decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising hidden failure paths on the production floor and deciding which risks require stronger controls.

ambition.what: Weekly sampling review for unstable production lines

tasks.altitude: The week contains less evidence collection and calculation, with more time spent observing process changes. Within existing authority, the manager can revise sampling sooner; batch-release rights do not expand.

reach.task: Schedule inspection capacity alongside production changes.
reach.learn: Production scheduling, bottleneck capacity and the cost of delayed testing.

evidence.claim: Sampling calculations and template assembly can use deterministic code once assumptions and rules are explicit.
Control-point selection still requires process knowledge and assessment of failure consequences.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size manufacturer with recorded defects, process maps and a quality approval process.
Time shares are estimates informed by the supplied priors; floor observation and risk judgement remain substantial.
Build ranges cover one production area with established statistical methods; broader validation may take longer.
GDPR applies where records identify workers. Consultation under national rules may be needed if collection changes worker monitoring.
unknowns: Available production interfaces and defect-record completeness.
Existing sampling standards and who may approve changes.
Product hazards, sector validation requirements and laboratory constraints.
Whether employee consultation is required for the proposed data use.
research_questions: Which existing configuration can already generate sampling plans?
Which statistical assumptions hold for each process and defect type?
Can historical results reproduce accepted sampling calculations?
new_work: Check missing records, stale process maps and unusual data distributions.
Maintain approved sampling rules and calculation versions.
Verify that released plans still match current production conditions.
tasks.statement: Identify critical points in the manufacturing process and specify sampling procedures to be used at these points.

tasks.short: Document testing procedures, methods and acceptance criteria.

steps.what: Gather approved criteria, method notes and validation evidence.
Write the procedure, including equipment, preparation, method steps and result recording.

loop.input: Approved criteria, method notes, validation evidence and controlled procedure template.
loop.output: Procedure draft with source references and explicitly marked gaps.
loop.check: Check required sections, units, identifiers and exact acceptance limits; require sources for technical instructions.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per procedure; unresolved technical gaps return to the author.
loop.why_not_simpler: Method notes contain varied prose that needs ordered instructions. Structured fields and standard sections use deterministic rendering.

steps.what: Check that instructions reproduce the validated method and resolve ambiguities.
Approve and release the procedure in the quality management system.
Email the release notice to affected production and laboratory teams.

tasks.design: An integration gathers approved sources from {DOCS} and the quality management system in {OTHER}; deterministic templates and a bounded drafting loop prepare a traceable procedure. Configured versioning, approval and release notifications publish the reviewed procedure and link it to implementation in {OPS_SYSTEM}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Authors repeatedly assembled source material and rewrote method notes, while release administration remained separate.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded drafting handles varied notes, while cheaper custom integration connects source versions and controlled templates. Existing document controls handle release.
tasks.still_hard: Incomplete method notes and instructions that sound plausible but fail in practice require technical review.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting ambiguous instructions and knowing what a technician needs to reproduce a validated test.

ambition.what: Illustrated setup instructions for newly assigned laboratory technicians

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from writing repeated sections to checking technical clarity and observing how technicians use instructions. The manager gains no new approval rights.

reach.task: Maintain controlled versions, retention records and links between procedures and evidence.
reach.learn: Document metadata, supersession rules and evidence traceability.

evidence.claim: Controlled templates, versioning and release notifications can be automated independently of technical approval.
Source-linked drafting can reduce document assembly while requiring review of technical instructions.

assumptions: Criteria and methods are already approved; this task documents them rather than inventing them.
The quality management system in {OTHER} holds validation evidence and supports controlled document release.
Build ranges cover one procedure family and existing approval roles.
GDPR applies to names and signatures in records. Consultation under national rules is assessed if acknowledgement tracking changes employee data use.
